decisions.reason: As a new supplement range closely aligned with the firm's consumer-health expansion and given visible standalone website support, its early performance likely meets or is close enough to aspiration levels for a large, growing firm with slack to keep it.
This skin and hair supplement builds directly on the established offer and was actively promoted at launch, so management would likely see no strong performance shortfall requiring withdrawal.

The joint-health supplement fits the firm's portfolio-broadening strategy and, despite more limited visibility than A or B, a large investing firm would usually continue it while results remain uncertain rather than drop it quickly.

This immune supplement appears more niche and had weaker website presence, which raises uncertainty, but the firm's organisational slack and willingness to broaden its portfolio still make retention more likely than withdrawal after only about a year.

Because this generic blood pressure medicine is described as more distant from the established offer and already faced a visible product problem in 2018, it is the clearest candidate to fall below aspiration levels and be discontinued so resources can be redirected.
